title: Boolean dimension of posets with planar cover graphs
formal: Does there exist an integer \(d\ge 1\) such that every finite poset \(\mathrm{P}=(V,<)\) with a planar undirected cover graph admits strict total orders \(\mathrm{L}_{1},\ldots ,\mathrm{L}_{d}\) on V and a Boolean function \(\varphi :\{0,1\}^{d}\to \{0,1\}\) satisfying, for all distinct \(x,y\in V, x<y\) if and only if \(\varphi (1[x<_{\mathrm{L}_{1}}y],\ldots ,1[x<_{\mathrm{L}_{d}}y])=1\)?
definitions: A finite poset is specified by an irreflexive transitive relation < on a finite set V. The undirected cover graph has vertex set V and an edge \(\{x,y\}\) when \(x<y\) with no z satisfying \(x<z<y\), or the reverse relation. Planarity means that this undirected graph has a drawing in the plane whose edge interiors do not intersect; an upward planar drawing of the order is not required. A strict total order compares every distinct pair in exactly one direction and is transitive. The orders \(\mathrm{L}_{i}\) need not extend the partial order. Each indicator \(1[x<_{\mathrm{L}_{i}}y]\) is a bit. Both the d orders and \(\varphi\) may depend on P, but the bound d is universal and independent of |V| and the height of P. The least possible number of orders is Boolean dimension. The claim is purely existential, with no algorithmic requirement.
answer_criterion: Prove the proposition in the problem statement or its logical negation with the stated model, hypotheses and quantifier order. The proof must settle the entire target. A result conditional on an additional assumption settles only that conditional version. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof checked by a proof assistant and matching this statement.
why: Determine whether planar cover structure permits a constant-size comparison description of an arbitrary partial order.

importance.reason: A constant-size Boolean description of every order with a planar cover graph would explain how planar local structure controls global order information.

progress.text: Blake, Micek and Trotter prove Boolean dimension at most 13 when the planar-cover-graph poset has a unique minimum.
The clique-width/dimension paper supplies related boundedness results but does not establish the target for all planar cover graphs.

context_blocks.text: A family of total orders supplies a short comparison signature for each ordered pair. Boolean dimension asks whether a single Boolean rule can reconstruct the partial-order relation from that signature. The orders are auxiliary encodings and need not respect every comparability.

Blake, Micek and Trotter connect this representation with reachability labeling and prove a constant bound under an additional unique-minimum assumption. That hypothesis is absent from the general question.
The underlying cover graph, rather than an upward planar drawing of the poset, is the specified planar object. Replacing one condition with the other would change the family of inputs.

sentences: The cover graph records immediate comparabilities of a finite partial order.
The question asks whether its planarity guarantees a constant number of total orders encoding every comparability.
One Boolean rule interprets the pairwise comparison bits from those orders.
The orders and rule may vary with the poset, but their number must have a universal bound.
The target links sparse graph structure to concise representations of reachability.

status_note: Reviewed through 11 September 2026. The unique-minimum theorem and related clique-width results do not resolve arbitrary planar cover graphs; no general resolution was found.

notes: Specified undirected cover-graph planarity, allowed orders that are not linear extensions, and a poset-dependent Boolean decoder.
